Mildred Johnson Randall operated a primary school on a Church plantation in Laie, Hawaii, in 1865 and 1873; she served without her husband. At the time, about 120 women accompanied husbands on missions while nearly 7,500 male missionaries served. (Matthew McBride, “‘Female Brethren’: Gender Dynamics in a Newly Integrated Missionary Force, 1898–1915,”Journal of Mormon History,vol. 44, no. 4 [Oct. 2018], 50.)
